plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 3-era timeline completes: 1823 (Michel Eugène Chevreul in Paris proves animal fats are triglyceride esters and explains how alkali saponification creates fatty-acid soap salts and glycerin) · 12 March 1891 (19-year-old Agnes Pockels in Brunswick measures water surface tension and surface films at her kitchen sink with a 70-cm tin trough and porcelain button, publishing in Nature with Lord Rayleigh) · 1913 & 1917–1935 (James William McBain at Bristol discovers spherical soap micelles, and Irving Langmuir and Katharine Blodgett at General Electric prove surface films are monolayers one molecule thick).

teach_overlay.detail: Animated timeline (1823 → 1935) alongside an inked summary of fat saponification, Agnes Pockels's kitchen-sink trough, spherical soap micelles, and single-molecule monolayers
teach_overlay.scale: from a Paris soap kettle and a German kitchen sink to single-molecule camera coatings and twenty-second virus-shattering handwashing, scientists proved that the most powerful chemistry in your home sits right beside your tap
